answers.answer: No. In SCOPe 2.08 (current release, frozen 2021-07-28), d1s9za_ (sunid 98768, PDB 1s9z chain A, protein 'Amyloidogenic design-1', sunid 103785) and d1hqja_ (sunid 61142, PDB 1hqj chain A, protein 'Unnamed design-1', sunid 100906) are placed in the same family k.40.1.1 'Designed trimeric coiled-coil' (family sunid 100905, superfamily k.40.1 sunid 100904, fold k.40 sunid 100903), but this shared family does NOT indicate homology. Both sit in class k 'Designed proteins' (sunid 58788), which SCOP/SCOPe explicitly treats as not a true class: classes h-l (coiled coils, low-resolution, peptides, designed proteins) are organizational conveniences, and their fold/superfamily/family nodes are not evolutionary units. In the true classes a-g, family co-membership asserts clear common ancestry and superfamily co-membership asserts probable common ancestry; in class k the hierarchy merely groups de novo designs by design type (here, synthetic trimeric coiled coils), so the usual family-level inference of homology cannot be applied. Both entries are de novo designs with no natural ancestor: 1s9z is a synthetic 17-residue peptide designed to form a native-like coiled coil at ambient temperature and amyloid-like fibrils when heated (PDB class 'de novo protein'), and 1hqj is a de novo designed trimeric coiled-coil peptide (PDB class 'de novo protein'). Any sequence or structural similarity between them (heptad-repeat hydrophobic core, parallel three-stranded alpha-helical bundle) reflects convergent application of the same coiled-coil design principles, not descent from a common ancestral gene, so the pair is analogous (shared designed architecture), not homologous. Limits and caveats: (1) do not transfer function between them, e.g. the amyloidogenic/fibril-forming behaviour of design-1 in 1s9z must not be attributed to the 1hqj design; (2) do not treat one as a homology-modelling template for the other on the basis of SCOPe family membership, nor use this pair as a positive homolog pair when benchmarking remote-homology detection; (3) because SCOPe groups class k by design type, the family also contains other independent designs (e.g. 'Unnamed design-2', sunid 100907), none of which are mutually homologous; (4) the SCOPe API returned no public ASTRAL sequence for either domain (both are short synthetic peptides), so I could not directly compare sequences, and the sunid records returned no comment text. The only external evidence that could bear on relatedness is the primary design literature for each PDB entry documenting that each sequence was designed independently (and whether either was derived from a common parent design such as a natural coiled-coil or an earlier synthetic scaffold); no amount of sequence/structure similarity alone would establish evolutionary homology for de novo proteins.
